record.frame: cad/part.py's frame, which is Pollen's mesh frame for pcb__raspberry_pi_zero_2_w.stl so the MJCF geom pos/quat place the board with no re-derivation: the board lies in the x-z plane, THICKNESS ALONG Y (y -0.8 .. +0.8), X the 65.0 mm length (-32.5 .. +32.5), Z the 30.0 mm width (-15.0 .. +15.0). +Y is the component side that carries the 40-pin header, and the header sits on the -Z half (cad/part.py HDR_Z = (-10.23, -12.77), i.e. centre Z = -11.50).
record.measurement_basis: Radxa publishes NO DXF and NO STEP for this board; §4 Mechanical Specification of the Product Brief (RAD-DOC-0084 Rev 1.10, 2026-06-26) is a RASTER drawing with no text layer, so every position below is a MEASUREMENT OF A PICTURE. Made 2026-09-02 by tools/measure_radxa_drawing.py; result in evidence/radxa-zero-3w-mechanical.json. Input: the copy in docs/fetched/radxa_zero_3w_product_brief.pdf, sha256 edfb01374bbc6ee4062adf50d5d7241de64b64c8e87d186b3577bbb8761ddead, page 6, embedded image 2480 x 1754 px composited with its SMask, nothing rescaled. Scale from the outline's own printed callouts 30.0 and 65.0 mm, edges located sub-pixel by ink-weighted centroid; the two axes agree to 0.0288 %, one pixel is 0.05321 mm. FOUR NEGATIVE CONTROLS pass on the same pixels: the 40-pin header body measures 5.1001 x 50.8187 mm where a 2x20 2.54 mm header is 5.08 x 50.80 (+0.020, +0.019), and its centre measures 3.3355 mm from one long edge and 32.4343 mm from one end where Radxa prints '3. 3' and '32. 4' (+0.036, +0.034). A wrong scale fails all four.
record.drawing_frame_D: Where a number is quoted 'from the left/top edge' it is in the drawing's own component-side view: origin at that view's top-left board corner, +X across the 30.0 mm width, +Y along the 65.0 mm length. D maps to part.py's frame as X_D -> -Z, Y_D -> X (sign not resolved; the board is symmetric to 0.066 mm about mid-length), Z_D -> +Y.

interfaces.name: mount_holes
interfaces.what: 4 × through-holes on a rectangular pattern, drilled along Y through the 1.6 mm board. CENTRES AT X = ±28.900 mm, Z = ±11.400 mm — the NOMINAL, reconstructed from Radxa's own printed callouts (edge inset '3. 6' on the printed outline '65. 0' × '30. 0'), which is what this record's own text argues is the better-supported figure and is therefore what it now uses. MEASURED diameter 2.8140 mm (sd 0.0125 over the four); Radxa prints '4 X Ø2. 8'. MEASURED pitch 57.8429 mm along X by 22.8662 mm along Z, i.e. centres at ±28.9215 / ±11.4331 — 0.0215 and 0.0331 mm from the nominal above, both inside the 0.0396 mm 1 sigma. MEASURED edge inset 3.5727 mm (sd 0.0396 over the eight edge distances); Radxa prints '3. 6' once. A nominal 3.600 mm inset reconstructs the two measured pitches to 57.800 / 22.800, i.e. within 0.043 and 0.066 mm (0.8 and 1.2 px) — the competing Raspberry-Pi-Zero nominal 58.000 / 23.000 is 0.157 and 0.134 mm out (3.0 and 2.5 px), so 3.6 is the better-supported nominal by a factor of 2 to 4. A Ø2.814 hole is a clearance hole for M2.5 (0.314 mm diametral clearance) and loose for M2 (0.814 mm).
interfaces.source: MEASURED 2026-09-02, tools/measure_radxa_drawing.py --check (4/4 negative controls PASS); result evidence/radxa-zero-3w-mechanical.json and out/measure/radxa-zero-3w-mechanical.json. Interchange arithmetic 2026-09-03, tools/check_board_hole_interchange.py -> out/measure/board-mount-interchange.json
interfaces.uncertainty_basis: 1 sigma of the eight measured edge insets, 0.0396 mm = 0.74 px on a raster whose pixel is 0.05321 mm. Radxa dimensions no hole position except the single '3. 6', so 3 dp cannot be had from this document — the ±28.900 / ±11.400 above are 3 dp of a 2-significant-figure callout, not 3 dp of measurement, and they carry ±0.0396 mm. A calipered production board, or a Radxa DXF/STEP, settles it.
interfaces.vs_the_pi_zero_2w_stand_in: FINDING 3, mechanical half — CORRECTED 2026-09-03, and the earlier sentence here was too generous. Pollen's MJCF carries a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W mesh whose drill measures 58.0 × 23.0 mm / Ø2.70 (cad/part.py MESH_MOUNT_*). The earlier text said 'an M2.5 screw absorbs all three [differences], so the printed head parts fit either board'. That was an adjective, not a check. tools/check_board_hole_interchange.py is the check — the screw is fixed by the printed post, so all float lives in the board's own hole and the test is hypot(Δpitch_long, Δpitch_wide)/2 <= (D_board_hole − d_screw)/2, with d_screw at its nominal maximum. Over the twelve directions (3 patterns × 2 boards × 2 screw sizes): 9 PASS, 1 CANNOT DETERMINE, 2 FAIL (out/measure/board-mount-interchange.json). ON M2 the claim holds everywhere — all six directions PASS with 0.2086 to 0.3676 mm of radial margin. ON M2.5, WHICH IS THE SIZE THESE HOLES ACTUALLY TAKE, it does not: a Pi Zero 2 W board on Radxa-pattern posts needs 0.1032 mm (measured pattern) or 0.1414 mm (nominal pattern) of radial offset and its Ø2.700 hole on a Ø2.500 screw gives only 0.1000 mm — short by 0.0032 mm and by 0.0414 mm of radius. FAIL, in both readings. The reverse direction, a Radxa board on Pi-Zero-pattern posts, fits by 0.0538 mm against the measured pattern but by only 0.0086 mm against the nominal one, which is inside the drawing's own 0.0396 mm 1 sigma: CANNOT DETERMINE. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE BUILD: nothing needs to change about the Radxa itself — the printed head part should be drilled on the RADXA pattern, because the Radxa is the specified board. What changes is the claim: the two patterns are not interchangeable, and a head printed for the Radxa will not take a Pi Zero 2 W on M2.5. It will on M2. AND THE BIGGER DIFFERENCE IS STILL NOT THE DRILL: what genuinely separates the boards is the CONNECTORS (2 × USB-C + micro-HDMI + 22-pin MIPI CSI here; micro-USB ×2 + mini-HDMI on a Pi Zero 2 W) — a shell-cutout problem, and it is the connector_edge_features interface's CANNOT DETERMINE.
interfaces.accepts_why: M2.5, not M2, and the two are no longer allowed to disagree between this field and the prose. THREE independent lines land on M2.5 for these four holes: (1) the measured hole itself — Ø2.8140 mm sits between ce-cad/cecad/fasteners.py's M2.5 close clearance (2.70) and its normal clearance (2.90), and gives 0.314 mm of diametral clearance on a Ø2.500 screw against 0.814 mm on a Ø2.000 one; (2) SPEC.md §4's hole census over Pollen's meshes, whose fourth population 'Ø2.7/2.8 ×20' is the only one of the four that is NOT an M2 figure; (3) docs/BOM.md §4, which buys 'M2.5×6 ×20' for exactly that population. connection:threaded-m2.5 was created in this repo on 2026-09-03 so this field could name a ref that resolves — before it existed the choice was a dangling ref or the M2 folder this hole is loose in. `bin/triad check connection:threaded-m2.5` PASSes (7 measured).

centres_mm.basis: NOMINAL from Radxa's printed '3. 6' edge inset on its printed 65.0 × 30.0 outline
centres_mm.why_nominal_is_the_record: The record must use its own best-supported figure. This interface's text already argues that the 3.600 mm inset reconstructs the measured ink 2-4x better than the Pi-Zero nominal does; carrying the raw half-pitch instead would publish the raster's noise as a design dimension. Both are kept: the nominal is what a drawing or a mate() should use, the measured is the evidence for it, and they differ by less than the measurement's own 1 sigma (0.0396 mm).

interfaces.confirmed_by_the_printed_part: FINDING 3 IS CLOSED BY A THIRD MEASUREMENT, and it is the one that matters — not the datasheet, not the placeholder mesh, but the PRINTED PART that holds the board. part:microduck-face-part's 'shell_screws' interface is 4 × Ø2.0500 × 4.0000 pilots at (x, z) = (±28.9200, 8.5650) and (±28.9200, 31.4350) — a 57.8400 × 22.8700 mm rectangle — each on a Ø6.0000 × 10.7000 boss with a Ø2.7000 × 1.0000 counterbore, MEASURED off Pollen's own face_part.stl by cecad.meshfeatures.cylinders (lane T, out/laneT/features/face_part.json). That rectangle is 0.0048 mm from THIS interface's measured pattern (57.8429 × 22.8662) and 0.2062 mm from the Pi Zero 2 W stand-in's (58.000 × 23.000) — a factor of 43. The printed part is drilled for the Radxa. The placeholder mesh is a placeholder. THE SCREW IS CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY TOO: Ø2.0500 is exactly the M2.5 tap drill in ce-cad/cecad/fasteners.py line 58 (M2's, line 57, is 1.60) and the Ø2.7000 counterbore is exactly that row's M2.5 close clearance — two features of the printed part on the M2.5 row, neither on the M2 row, which is why this interface accepts connection:threaded-m2.5. NOTE FOR WHOEVER OWNS ce-parts/microduck-face-part: that interface is named 'shell_screws' and declares accepts ['connection:threaded-m2']. On this measurement it is neither a shell screw nor an M2. It was NOT edited from this lane. Artifact: out/measure/board-mount-interchange.json, which_board_is_the_printed_part_drilled_for.

interfaces.name: header_40pin
interfaces.what: 2x20 GPIO header on 2.54 mm pitch. Body rectangle MEASURED 5.1001 mm across the width by 50.8187 mm along the length (nominal 5.08 x 50.80). Its centreline sits 3.3355 mm from one long board edge — Radxa prints '3. 3' — which places it at Z = -(15.0 - 3.3355) = -11.6645 in this frame, against the stand-in mesh's -11.50; and 32.4343 mm from one end — Radxa prints '32. 4' — i.e. 0.0657 mm off mid-length, taken as X = 0. Origin is the body centre on the component-side face (Y = +0.8, the top of the 1.6 mm board).
interfaces.source: MEASURED 2026-09-02, tools/measure_radxa_drawing.py; these four numbers are the tool's own negative controls
interfaces.pin_map: electrical.host.json record.header_40pin — verdict PASS, two independent vendor pages (brief §6.1.1 p.6 and the Radxa wiki) agree on every listed pin
interfaces.cannot_determine: WHICH CORNER IS PIN 1, and the header insulator height above the PCB. Neither is dimensioned in §4, neither is on the wiki. A calipered board settles both. A HAT laid out with pin 1 at the wrong end is a scrapped board, so this is not a cosmetic gap.

interfaces.name: board_envelope
interfaces.what: 65.000 x 30.000 mm PCB outline, R3.0 corners, centred on the origin, thickness 1.6 mm along Y. 65.0 and 30.0 are Radxa's own printed callouts ('65. 0', '30. 0', §4 p.5). R3.0 and 1.6 are MEASURED off Pollen's Pi-Zero-2-W stand-in mesh (cad/part.py CORNER_R, T) and are NOT stated by Radxa anywhere in RAD-DOC-0084.
interfaces.cannot_determine: PCB THICKNESS, CORNER RADIUS and BOARD MASS are in no fetched Radxa document. The 1.6 mm / R3.0 carried here are the stand-in mesh's. A calipered board and a scale settle all three; the mass matters because the whole robot is 780 g and the compute board's share is currently unmeasured.

interfaces.name: connector_edge_features
interfaces.what: §4's component-side view carries five more callouts that dimension connector/feature lines and label none of them: '12. 5', '41. 5', '54. 7' and '14. 4' along the length, '15. 5' across the width. The sweep found feature lines at 54.5186 and 54.8379 mm from the top edge (bracketing the printed 54.7) and vertical lines 4.9425 and 20.4285 mm from the left edge (15.486 mm apart — the printed 15.5). The p.3 photo names the ports (USB 2.0 OTG Type-C, USB 3.0 Host Type-C, micro-HDMI, MIPI CSI, micro-SD, maskrom button, antenna connector) but is not dimensioned, so no callout could be attached to a named connector.
interfaces.why: This is exactly the interface a head-shell cutout needs, and it is the one Radxa leaves unlabelled. NOTE: '54. 7' was previously read as the mounting-hole pitch along the length and written into cad/part.py as RADXA_LONG_SPAN; it is not — the hole pitch measures 57.8429 mm. Corrected 2026-09-02.
interfaces.what_settles_it: a Radxa DXF or STEP for the ZERO 3W (none published as of 2026-09-02), or a calipered production board
